Find the solution $(p,q)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-4p-5q=1 \\ 4p+2q=2\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
Find the solution $(a,b)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3a-b=2 \\ -3a+2b=-1\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $a$ in the first equation is $3,$ and the coefficient of $a$ in the second equation is $-3.$ 

Since these numbers add to zero, we can add the two equations, *eliminate* the variable $a,$ and solve the resulting equation for $b\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{3a}-b & =2 \\ -\cancel{3a}+2b & =-1 \\ (-b+2b) & =(2+(-1)) \\ b & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $b=1.$ However, we still need to find $a.$ To do this, we substitute $b=1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-b & =2 \\ 3a-(1) & =2 \\ 3a & =3 \\ a & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=1, \,b=1,$ which can be expressed as $\left(1,1\right).$
